Hi, girls! I am so glad to see you!
Whoa, Sasha, tell me, are you pregnant?
Well of course I am pregnant, does it not show?
Alright, I will go say hello to all the guys.
Hi, Sasha! How beautiful you have become!
I am so glad to see all of you too!
Pregnancy really only makes you more beautiful.
Well, how is Ilya? Is he getting ready to become a father?
Wait, Max, what does Ilya have to do with this?

meanings.en: in the presence of, in front of (a person)
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in the presence of, in front of; at, under', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Чтобы строго фиксировать, когда сотрудник приходит.
examples.trans: To strictly record when an employee arrives.

examples.text: Но, к сожалению, тебе придётся это проглотить.
examples.trans: But unfortunately, you will have to swallow this.

examples.text: Привет, Макс! Я подумала, ты меня избегаешь.
examples.trans: Hi, Max! I thought you were avoiding me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Здесь только я решаю, что можно делать!
examples.trans: Here only I decide what is allowed!

examples.text: Никто не имеет права здесь ничего менять!
examples.trans: Nobody has the right to change anything here!

examples.text: Здесь только я всё решаю!
examples.trans: Only I decide everything here!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Перемены могут начаться абсолютно в любой момент.
examples.trans: Changes can begin at absolutely any moment.

examples.text: Они всегда застают тебя совсем врасплох.
examples.trans: They always catch you completely off guard.

examples.text: Доброе утро, Виктор Петрович, вы сегодня опаздываете.
examples.trans: Good morning, Viktor Petrovich, you are late today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sense, meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В смысле Маша? Извини, Марина, то есть Эльвира!
examples.trans: You mean Masha? Sorry, Marina, I mean Elvira!

examples.text: В каком смысле при чём здесь Илья?
examples.trans: What do you mean what does Ilya have to do with this?

examples.text: В том смысле, что мы с ним разошлись.
examples.trans: In the sense that he and I broke up.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Витя, ты пьяный, немедленно прекрати этот шум!
examples.trans: Vitya, you are drunk, stop this circus immediately!

examples.text: И будем весело прыгать через этот костёр!
examples.trans: And we will merrily jump over this bonfire!

examples.text: Оставить этот ресторан французским и сохранить весь персонал.
examples.trans: To keep this restaurant French and retain all the staff.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы стали частью большой ресторанной сети.
examples.trans: We have become part of a large restaurant chain.

examples.text: Мы что, теперь на заводе работаем?
examples.trans: What, do we work at a factory now?

examples.text: Расслабься, мы теперь просто работаем вместе.
examples.trans: Relax, we just work together now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'him', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Они всегда застают тебя совсем врасплох.
examples.trans: They always catch you completely off guard.

examples.text: Я не понял, это что за шлагбаум?
examples.trans: I do not understand, what is this barrier?

examples.text: Вот твой новый электронный пропуск, держи.
examples.trans: Here is your new electronic pass, take it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'ойтись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke up / parted ways'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и разойтись вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and broke up on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют разойтись.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to broke up.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: С чего ты решил, что ребёнок от Ильи?
examples.trans: What made you think that the baby is Ilya's?

examples.text: Суд решил.
examples.trans: The court has decided.

examples.text: Я решил.
examples.trans: I've decided.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: С чего ты решил, что ребёнок от Ильи?
examples.trans: What made you think that the baby is Ilya's?

examples.text: Это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: This is my child.

examples.text: Ребёнок спит.
examples.trans: The child is asleep.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот твой новый электронный пропуск, держи.
examples.trans: Here is your new electronic pass, take it.

examples.text: Мы что, теперь на заводе работаем?
examples.trans: What, do we work at a factory now?

examples.text: Чтобы строго фиксировать, когда сотрудник приходит.
examples.trans: To strictly record when an employee arrives.

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ты её только сильнее разозлишь, давай лучше я.
examples.trans: You will only anger her more, let me do it instead.

examples.text: Давай лучше я с ней поговорю.
examples.trans: Let me talk to her instead.

examples.text: Давай, Федя, смелее говори всё шефу.
examples.trans: Go on, Fedya, boldly tell the Chef everything.
